guarantees.claim: c[0] is driven as the XOR of r and scale_omega2_b_buf.
c[1] is driven as the XOR of c_buf[0] and scale_omega2_q_buf.
c[2] is driven as the XOR of c_buf[1] and mul_b1_b0_buf.
c[3] is driven as the XOR of c_buf[2] and mul_b1_q0_buf.
c[4] is driven as the XOR of c_buf[3] and mul_b0_q1_buf.
c[5] is driven as the XOR of c_buf[4] and mul_q1_q0_buf.

assumptions.claim: The input signals r, c_buf[4:0], scale_omega2_b_buf, scale_omega2_q_buf, mul_b1_b0_buf, mul_b1_q0_buf, mul_b0_q1_buf, mul_q1_q0_buf are correctly computed masked shares that maintain the intended masking and correctness of the GF(2^4) inverse operation.
assumptions.cond: Whenever the inverse is being computed.
assumptions.risk: If these inputs violate the masking property (e.g., due to a logic error in the preceding masked multiplication stages), the output c may become unmasked and leak secret information through side-channels.

uncertain_points.claim: The chunk performs no integrity check on input signals; any fault (e.g., single-event upset, laser injection) on the input signals directly propagates to the output c without detection.
uncertain_points.cond: When a fault occurs on any of the input signals during operation.
uncertain_points.risk: Fault injection could corrupt the AES S-box output, leading to incorrect ciphertext or plaintext, potentially enabling differential fault analysis.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational XOR tree may exhibit glitches if input signals arrive at different times due to varying logic depths from preceding stages, potentially exposing intermediate values.
uncertain_points.cond: During signal transitions at the inputs.
uncertain_points.risk: Glitches on c could leak masked share relationships and reduce side-channel resistance.
